ranking.method: Rank candidate and conditional groups separately by the mean of three crop median longest dry runs (<1 mm/day); higher exposure of the two completion-optimized schedules; ties by branch_id ascending; spell length is not normalized away.
notes: Candidate group is empty; no candidate branches were ranked.
Climate views use only common complete historical seasons; missing evidence and branches without a common season set are unranked.
Three crop summaries are equally weighted as a disclosed product convention; this is not duration neutrality or agricultural suitability.

temperature.match: distance from the crop profile's EcoCrop temperature optimum range; 0 when the seasonal median is inside the range
temperature.source: FAO EcoCrop database, OpenCLIM mirror EcoCrop_DB.csv (https://github.com/OpenCLIM/ecocrop)
temperature.applicability: published general species/crop-level EcoCrop range; not variety- or stage-specific
temperature.seasonal_matching: project-defined median of daily T2M over the realized growing period
temperature.ordering: lower median seasonal distance is closer to guidance
temperature.tolerance: reported as context only; not used for ordering
temperature.scope: general crop guidance, not variety- or stage-specific damage

dry_spell.statistic: longest consecutive dry-day run within one crop period
dry_spell.scope: growing-period exposure, not inherent drought tolerance

heavy_rain.statistic: heavy-rain days per valid growing day
heavy_rain.scope: meteorological exposure, not crop damage or waterlogging

definitions.common_seasons: only seasons with complete daily T2M and PRECTOTCORR for every crop in both completion-optimized schedules
definitions.schedules: min_realization and max_realization are completion-optimized examples; ordering uses the higher exposure of the two, not a worst-case bound over all possible schedules

limitations: Temperature uses general EcoCrop optimum/tolerance guidance; it is not a stage-specific daily damage threshold or a variety validation.
Dry spell and heavy rain are growing-period adaptations of meteorological indices, not standard annual Climdex outputs and not crop-damage predictions.
Rainfall totals are descriptive context; no irrigation demand is inferred and no rainfall-minus-demand calculation is made.
GWETTOP is regional MERRA-2 surface wetness context, not root-zone moisture or a crop threshold.
Equal weighting of the three crop summaries is a disclosed product convention, not proof of duration neutrality or agricultural suitability.
Missing days are excluded; they are never treated as zero rain or joined across gaps.
